editions.headline: Drones Strike Northern Iraq and Sirens Sound in Bahrain After a 13th Night of U.S. Strikes on Iran — Wall Street Closes a Volatile Week Little Changed as Oil Pulls Back From $100
editions.teaser: Explosive-laden drones target Irbil in northern Iraq and sirens sound in Bahrain and Jordan Friday after U.S. Central Command completes a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with fresh strikes reported on a Revolutionary Guard naval base, Qeshm Island, and sites in Isfahan and Khuzestan provinces; President Trump says he is weighing further escalation after Tehran rejected an Iraqi-brokered ceasefire proposal, even as he separately says Iran is “getting more serious” about talks; Wall Street closes a volatile week little changed, with the S&P 500 up 0.05% to 7,411.98, the Dow gaining 0.46% to 51,947.25, and the Nasdaq slipping 0.64% to 24,975.82 as a 3.5% jump in Apple offsets continued chip-sector weakness; Brent crude pulls back below $96 and WTI falls to $90.12 after briefly topping $100 Thursday, even as all three indexes finish the week lower; Fed rate-hike odds for the July 29 meeting hold near 38%, up from just 10.7% a week ago, as Chair Kevin Warsh's first live-hike test approaches; Bitcoin slips to around $64,029; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage holds at a one-year-high 6.58%; the Cubs rally past the Pirates 3-2 in 10 innings on a Dansby Swanson go-ahead single to improve to 58-45, while the White Sox fall to the Astros 9-5 but remain alone atop the AL Central at 54-48; Chicago enjoys a mild, partly sunny Saturday near 83°F before the weekend heat builds toward the low 90s.

editions.headline: Trump Threatens a “Massive Attack, Bigger Than Ever Before” as Iran Rejects a Ceasefire Offer and Oil Tops $100 — Tesla and Alphabet Selloff Sends Wall Street to Its Worst Day in a Month
editions.teaser: President Trump tells Axios he is weighing a “massive attack” on Iran, “bigger than ever before,” after Tehran rejects an Iraqi-mediated ceasefire proposal and U.S. strikes hit Iran for a 13th consecutive night; Iran retaliates on U.S.-linked targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, while Yemen's Houthi rebels claim fresh Red Sea attacks on Saudi shipping and Reuters reports Iran flew IRGC commanders into Yemen this month; Brent crude briefly topped $100 a barrel Thursday for the first time since May before easing toward $97; Wall Street closed Thursday at S&P 500 7,408.30 (−1.21%), Nasdaq 25,137.69 (−2.15%), Dow 51,711.65 (−0.97%), its worst session in a month, as Tesla cratered 14.5% on an earnings miss and negative free cash flow and Alphabet fell 7% despite beating on revenue after raising 2026 capex guidance to $205 billion; Fed hike odds for July 29 climbed toward 40% as the oil shock revives inflation fears; Bitcoin holds near $65,030 as gold pulls back to around $4,049; the White Sox host the Astros tonight alone atop the AL Central at 54-47, and the Cubs open a series at Pittsburgh at 57-45; Chicago enjoys a mostly sunny, pleasant Friday near 84°F.

editions.headline: Trump Vows to Bomb an Iranian Bridge or Power Plant for Every Ship Iran Hits in Hormuz as Houthis Strike Saudi Tankers and the War's Price Tag Hits $37.5 Billion
editions.teaser: President Trump warns the U.S. will destroy one Iranian bridge or power plant, including in Tehran, for every future attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, as U.S. Central Command completes a 12th consecutive night of strikes and Yemen's Houthi rebels claim attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, opening a second maritime front; Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth tells the Senate the war has cost $37.5 billion so far and seeks $67 billion more; Brent crude tops $98 and WTI climbs above $90, six-week highs, as Alphabet beats on earnings but raises 2026 capex to $205 billion (shares down premarket) and Tesla posts its first negative free-cash-flow quarter in two years; Wall Street closed Wednesday at S&P 500 7,498.96 (-0.14%), Nasdaq 25,690.90 (-0.57%), Dow 52,218.58 (-0.01%); Fed hike odds for July 29 climb to roughly 36% as the oil shock complicates Chair Warsh's path; Bitcoin holds near $65,659 as gold gains 1.5% to $4,137; the White Sox beat the Rangers 4-2 to move alone atop the AL Central (54-47) while the Cubs fall to the Tigers 5-1 in their series finale (57-45); Chicago enjoys a mostly sunny, pleasant Thursday near 78°F with low humidity.

editions.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran for an 11th Straight Night as the Campaign Widens to Tehran's Outskirts — Houthis Open a New Front With a Saudi Blockade
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command completes its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, for the first time reaching the outskirts of Tehran and a military site near Tabriz in a departure from the campaign's earlier focus on southern Iran; Iran retaliates on U.S.-linked sites in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, while Houthi rebels in Yemen declare a new naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, threatening the kingdom's Red Sea pipeline workaround; Pakistan hosts Iran's interior minister for revived diplomacy as Secretary of State Rubio says Tehran isn't "serious about talks"; oil jumps to 5-6 week highs (WTI ~$87, Brent ~$94) on the escalation; Wall Street closed Tuesday at S&P 500 7,509.20 (+0.89%), Nasdaq 25,837.21 (+1.29%), Dow ~52,223 (+0.74%) as chips rebounded, with Wednesday futures easing ahead of Alphabet and Tesla earnings after the close; CME FedWatch shows ~24% odds of a July 29 hike and ~69% odds of at least one hike by September as Cleveland Fed's Hammack joins the hawks; Bitcoin holds near $65,900; 30-year mortgage steady at 6.57% as existing home sales unexpectedly fell 2.4% in June; the Cubs rout the Tigers 11-2 to even their series (57-44) while the White Sox are blanked 10-0 by the Rangers with catcher Kyle Teel headed to the IL (53-47); Chicago sees a cooler, clearer Wednesday near 76°F as air quality improves, with a Beach Hazard Statement in effect for Lake Michigan.

editions.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran for a 10th Consecutive Night as Wall Street Looks Past the War Toward a Marquee Earnings Week
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command carries out a tenth straight night of strikes on Iran, hitting military command centers, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defense systems, with explosions reported in Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, Shiraz, Isfahan, Bandar Lengeh, Chabahar, and Konarak; the IRGC claims retaliatory strikes on U.S.-linked targets in Kuwait and Bahrain and says two more tankers were disabled in the Strait of Hormuz, while Jordan intercepts five Iranian drones; Trump warns on Truth Social that Iran "will pay for that killing many times over," and the U.S. death toll holds at 18 after a brutal weekend, with a Dover AFB dignified transfer postponed; Wall Street mostly looks past the war as chip stocks rebound (Nasdaq 100 futures +1.3%, KOSPI +3.6%) and 3M and GM both beat earnings estimates ahead of Alphabet, Tesla, Intel and IBM reporting later this week; oil eases from Monday's spike (WTI ~$82.56, Brent ~$88-90) on reports Iran is weighing mediator proposals; Bitcoin climbs back above $66,000 as Cleveland Fed's Hammack joins hawkish voices pushing December hike odds to 80%; the White Sox rout the Rangers 10-3 to snap a 10-game Globe Life skid (53-46) while the Cubs fall to the Tigers 8-6 in 10 innings (56-44); Chicago sees hazy skies near 84°F with air quality improving toward moderate and another late-day storm chance before a cooler midweek.

editions.headline: U.S. Death Toll Hits 18 as Ninth Night of Strikes Pounds Iran — Wall Street Shrugs It Off Again as Chips Rebound and Oil Pares a 4% Spike
editions.teaser: The Pentagon confirms a third U.S. service member died over the weekend disposing of a downed Iranian drone in northern Iraq, pushing the American death toll to 18 and closing out the war's worst 72-hour stretch for U.S. forces after Friday's fatal strike on Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti Air Base; CENTCOM recovers the remains of the previously missing soldier as the U.S. launches a ninth straight night of strikes and surges additional F-16s and F-35s into the region even as officials warn munitions stockpiles are thinning; Iran retaliates by striking Jordan's Aqaba airport, U.S.-linked bases in Kuwait, and targets in Syria, while the IRGC claims two tankers were “forced to cease movement” in the Strait of Hormuz and Kuwait's desalination plant is hit for a second straight day; Trump says Iran has been “very, very badly damaged,” while Rubio says the U.S. remains open to diplomacy as Iran signals it will weigh mediator proposals, pulling Brent back from an overnight spike to $90.79 and WTI back from $84.68; Wall Street mostly shrugs it off, with the S&P 500 up 0.63%, Nasdaq up 1.02%, and Dow up 0.23% at midday as chips rebound into a heavy earnings week; gas prices top a national $4/gallon average; Andy Burnham is sworn in as UK prime minister; Armstrong Economics warns “wars end with an invoice” as the IMF cuts global growth to ~3%, and reports Iran has warned UAE airports to prepare for evacuation; the Cubs (56-43) rout the Twins 10-1 behind Imanaga's seven shutout innings and the White Sox (52-46) blank the Blue Jays 3-0 to take the series, with both clubs opening new series today; Chicago sees hazy skies near 84°F with an air quality alert through tonight and a slight risk of severe storms this evening, damaging winds the top concern.

editions.headline: Iran Declares the MOU “Suspended” After an Eighth Night of U.S. Strikes as the American Death Toll Climbs to 16
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command carries out an eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iran early Sunday, hitting an under-construction nuclear power plant near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island, as Tehran declares the 60-day memorandum of understanding “suspended” following Friday's deadliest attack yet: two U.S. service members killed and a third missing after Iran struck Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, bringing the American death toll in the war to 16; Kuwait's power and desalination plant is hit for a second straight day, and Bahrain and Kuwait both report intercepting fresh Iranian aerial attacks Sunday morning; Wall Street closed Friday on its worst week in months (S&P 500 -1.01% to 7,457.69, Nasdaq -1.40% to 25,520.24, Dow -406.55 to 52,146.42; week: S&P -1.6%, Nasdaq -2.9%) as the PHLX Semiconductor Index confirmed a bear market; oil surged into the weekend, with Brent settling at $88.10 (+4.6%, +16% on the week) and WTI at $82.49 (+4.5%); Bitcoin holds near $64,850, up from Friday's $62,810 low; gold ticks back above $4,000 to ~$4,017; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage holds at 6.55%, a third straight weekly increase, as NAR reports June's median existing home price hit a record $440,600; the White Sox (51-46) stay alone in first place in the AL Central after a 1-0 loss to Toronto Saturday, and the Cubs (55-43) bounce back 6-2 over the Twins, with both clubs playing series finales today; Chicago sees hazy sunshine and mid-80s with an Air Quality Alert extended through Monday for wildfire smoke, ahead of a severe storm threat Monday.

editions.headline: Iran War Fallout Deepens Into the Weekend as 10,000 Lose Water and Bahrain Intercepts Fresh Strikes — Wall Street Closes Its Worst Week in Months
editions.teaser: Iran's national water company says roughly 10,000 people across 20 villages are without water after Friday night's seventh consecutive round of U.S. strikes, which hit bridges, a railway junction, and an airport near Bandar Abbas, as Iran's Health Ministry puts the toll since July 6 at 50+ killed and 500+ wounded; Bahrain's air defenses intercept a fresh wave of Iranian attacks Saturday after Kuwait reported a fire at a power and desalination plant; Wall Street closes its worst week in months (S&P -1.6%, Nasdaq -2.9%, Dow -0.9% for the week; Friday: S&P -1.01% to 7,457.69, Nasdaq -1.40% to 25,520.24, Dow -406.55 to 52,146.42) as the PHLX Semiconductor Index confirms a bear market, down 20.2% from its June 22 record on Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model release and continued fallout from Netflix's weak guide and TSMC's raised capex; President Trump accuses China of 2020 election interference in a Thursday address, declassifying documents Beijing calls "entirely fabricated," straining the U.S.-China trade truce; Bitcoin recovers to ~$64,100 over the weekend after Friday's $62,810 low; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rises to 6.55%, a third straight weekly increase; the White Sox (51-45) rout the Blue Jays 12-4 to stand alone in first place in the AL Central, while the Cubs (54-43) fall to the Twins 5-2 with a rematch today at Wrigley; Chicago sees a warm, hazy Saturday with a high near 87° and a 54% chance of isolated afternoon storms.

editions.headline: Seventh Day of Strikes Hits Iranian Bridges and Rail as Tehran Strikes Al Udeid and Kuwait — Chip Selloff Deepens as Netflix Slides on Weak Q3 Guide
editions.teaser: U.S. strikes hit bridges, a railway junction, and an airport across Hormozgan and Sistan-Baluchestan provinces overnight, killing at least seven to eight and severing routes out of Bandar Abbas, as Iran retaliates by striking Qatar's Al Udeid Air Base (wounding four, including a child) and hitting power and desalination infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain, with a tanker struck off Oman and U.S. Marines boarding another vessel in the contested Strait of Hormuz; oil climbs roughly 2% on the escalation, with Brent near $85.76 and WTI near $80.64; U.S. futures point lower (S&P -0.8%, Nasdaq 100 -1.6% to -1.9%) after Thursday's chip-led selloff (S&P -0.51% to 7,533.77, Nasdaq -1.47%) deepens on TSMC's raised 2026 capex guidance ($60-64B) and a weak Netflix Q3 revenue outlook that sent shares down more than 8% after hours; Bitcoin slips to about $62,800; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rises to 6.55%, its third straight weekly increase; gold eases to $3,994 and silver falls nearly 3% per Armstrong's Market Talk; the Cubs (54-42) host the Twins and the White Sox (50-45) open a series at Toronto as both return from the All-Star break; Chicago faces a hot, humid Friday with a high near 87° and heat index values up to 95, with a 50% chance of scattered afternoon storms.

editions.headline: Sixth Night of Strikes Brings Sirens to Bahrain and Kuwait as Trump Weighs Seizing Iran's Main Oil Terminal — UnitedHealth's Blowout Offsets a Chip Wobble
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command strikes Iran for a sixth straight day and disables a tanker headed for Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil export terminal, as CNN reports Trump is weighing options to expand the operation, including potentially seizing the island itself; air raid sirens sound in Bahrain and Kuwait, Iran's army confirms at least seven military personnel killed, and Trump says Iran released an American woman detained since December 2024 as a "gesture of goodwill"; UnitedHealth Group jumps 7% premarket on an earnings beat and raised guidance, with GE Aerospace and J.B. Hunt also topping estimates, but S&P 500 futures slip 0.2-0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures fall about 1% after Taiwan Semiconductor's raised capex guidance overshadows its beat, dragging SK Hynix down 11% and Samsung over 7% in Seoul; Fed Chair Kevin Warsh wraps two days of congressional testimony pledging to "follow the law and follow the data"; Bitcoin holds near $64,750, up about 4% on the week; WTI trades near $79.70 and Brent near $84.60 as oil stays elevated; the IRS rolls out Automatic Exemption from Penalty (AEP), replacing First-Time Abate for compliant filers; Freddie Mac's weekly mortgage survey is due at noon with Zillow's daily tracker already up to 6.49%; the Cubs (54-42, No. 1 NL Wild Card) and White Sox (50-45, tied atop the AL Central) sit out the final day of the All-Star break with the August 3 trade deadline approaching; Chicago is under an Air Pollution Action Day with the AQI forecast to exceed 150 and highs near the mid-90s.

editions.headline: Fifth Night of Strikes Collides With Warsh's Senate Showdown — Cooling PPI and a $65K Bitcoin Breakout Lift Wall Street
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command strikes Iran for a fifth straight day and redirects two vessels attempting to run the reinstated Hormuz naval blockade in its first 17 hours, as Iran says U.S. strikes have killed 30+ civilians and confirms retaliatory strikes on U.S.-linked bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan; Trump abandons his proposed 20% Hormuz transit toll in favor of Gulf state trade deals; Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's second day of Senate Banking testimony turns adversarial when Elizabeth Warren accuses him of a tone that "seems to invite corruption" over an unanswered blackout-period question, and Warsh responds by pledging to "follow the law and follow the data"; June PPI falls 0.3% m/m and the Empire State Manufacturing Index jumps to a four-year-high 15.6, with FedWatch pricing 85.6% odds of a July hold; S&P 500 holds near 7,562 (+0.25%), Nasdaq +0.47%, as ASML's raised guidance gives way to a reversal in Micron (-7-9%) while Morgan Stanley and BlackRock beat on earnings; Bitcoin tops $65,000 for the first time since June 17, up over 4% on cooling inflation data, with Ethereum crossing $1,900; Bankrate's 30-year mortgage holds at 6.59% as Freddie Mac's weekly reading stays at 6.49% ahead of Thursday's update; the AL shuts out the NL 4-0 in the All-Star Game as White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas homers in the eighth and Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong singles, with both Chicago clubs off until Friday; Chicago remains under an Air Quality Alert through midnight with highs near 97° and a heat index well above 100°.

editions.headline: US and Iran Trade a Third Night of Strikes as CENTCOM Preps to Reimpose the Hormuz Blockade — Cooling CPI and a Bank Earnings Wall Collide on Wall Street
editions.teaser: US Central Command carries out a third straight night of strikes on Iran, using one-way attack sea drones for the first time, as Iran strikes two UAE-flagged tankers with cruise missiles inside Omani waters, killing one crew member; CENTCOM says it will reinstate the Hormuz naval blockade at 4 PM ET Tuesday and Trump floats a 20% transit toll; Brent tops $86 (one-month high) after settling Monday at $83.30 (+9.59%), its biggest jump in six years, while WTI nears $80 after a $78.14 Monday settle; June CPI cools sharply to 3.5% y/y from May's 4.2%, down 0.4% m/m — the largest monthly drop since April 2020 — just 90 minutes before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first semiannual testimony to the House Financial Services Committee; JPMorgan ($16.9B profit, EPS $6.14), Wells Fargo (+22% net income), Bank of America (+27% profit) and Goldman Sachs (EPS $20.98, shares +4%) all beat, while IBM plunges over 22% on weak revenue; S&P 500 +0.3% and Nasdaq +1% as chips rebound from Monday's KOSPI-driven rout; Bitcoin holds near $62,780, gold slips to ~$4,010; Bankrate's 30-year mortgage hits a one-month-high 6.64% while Freddie Mac's weekly read holds at 6.49%; Cardinals rookie Jordan Walker stuns Philadelphia to win the Home Run Derby over Kyle Schwarber 12-11 as Munetaka Murakami is eliminated in Round 1; both the White Sox (50-45, first in the AL Central) and Cubs (54-42, second in the NL Central) sit out the All-Star break, with Pete Crow-Armstrong, Miguel Vargas, Murakami and Tristan Peters representing Chicago at tonight's Midsummer Classic in Philadelphia; Chicagoland's heat wave peaks today with highs in the low-to-mid 90s and a heat index near 100.

editions.headline: US and Iran Trade Fresh Strikes Overnight as Both Sides Dispute Whether the Strait of Hormuz Is Actually Open
editions.teaser: US Central Command carries out a fresh round of overnight strikes on Iran, using one-way attack sea drones for the first time, as Iran continues to insist the Strait of Hormuz is closed "until further notice" while CENTCOM maintains it remains open; Bloomberg tracking shows commodity carriers crossing the strait with AIS transponders switched off, with "dark" crossings now outnumbering tracked ones for three straight days; Brent crude spikes to $79.29 before paring to ~$78.14, WTI touches $74.41 before settling near $73; Polymarket prices just 22% odds of an "up" S&P open Monday, and futures fall sharply before the cash market opens mixed (Dow +0.21%, S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.86%) as KOSPI plunges 9% and Nikkei falls nearly 2% overnight; Bitcoin holds near $63,050, gold slips 1.1% to $4,074.57 despite the war headlines; Warsh testifies before the House Financial Services Committee Tuesday with June CPI landing 90 minutes prior, and JPMorgan, BofA, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Citigroup all report Tuesday; Bankrate's 30-year mortgage hits 6.58% Monday while Freddie Mac's weekly read holds at 6.49%; both the White Sox (50-45, first in the AL Central) and Cubs (54-42, second in the NL Central) enter the All-Star break after series wins, with Pete Crow-Armstrong, Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami and Tristan Peters representing Chicago in Tuesday's Midsummer Classic; Chicagoland's second heat wave of the summer arrives today with a high near 90°F, building into the low 90s through Friday.

editions.headline: Iran Closes the Strait of Hormuz and Strikes Five Gulf Nations as the US Answers With a Third Round of Airstrikes
editions.teaser: Iran's IRGC disables the Cyprus-flagged container ship GFS Galaxy near Oman and declares the Strait of Hormuz closed "until further notice," prompting a third round of US airstrikes on roughly 140 Iranian targets; Tehran retaliates with missile and drone strikes on Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan and Oman, wounding three in Qatar and landing missiles in Jordan, as Ghalibaf declares "the era of one-sided deals is OVER"; CENTCOM insists Iran does not control the strait; Wall Street remains closed for the weekend after Friday's S&P 500 close of 7,575.39 on SK Hynix's blockbuster Nasdaq debut, with oil and equity futures set to reopen Sunday evening for the first real read on the escalation; Bitcoin holds near $63,800; Fed Chair Warsh testifies before the House Tuesday with June CPI landing 90 minutes prior; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate rose to 6.49%; White Sox (49-45) blank the Athletics 1-0 to stay in first place in the AL Central, Cubs (53-42) rally past the Reds 5-3; Chicago enjoys one more sunny day before Monday's heat wave builds in.

editions.headline: Trump Says the Ceasefire Is "Over" but Iran Talks Will Continue — Wall Street Closes the Week Near Records on SK Hynix's Blockbuster Debut
editions.teaser: Trump insists the U.S.-Iran ceasefire remains "over" even as both sides agree to keep talking, with Iran's Ghalibaf saying "we have no trust in you" and a CNN/ISIS analysis finding apparent nuclear-site reconstruction at Parchin and activity at Pickaxe Mountain during the ceasefire window; Wall Street shrugs it off as SK Hynix's $26.5B Nasdaq debut (largest-ever U.S. listing by a foreign company) headlines a Friday close of records-adjacent gains (S&P +0.42% to 7,575.39, Nasdaq +0.29% to 26,281.61, Dow +0.29% to 52,637.01); Bitcoin reclaims $64K; Freddie Mac's 30-year hits 6.49% as NAR reports a record $440,600 median home price; the Kwong COVID-era Form 843 refund window closed Thursday; White Sox (48-45) rout the Athletics 14-1 to take first in the AL Central, Cubs (52-42) are shut out by Hunter Greene; Chicago enjoys one more mild sunny weekend before next week's heat wave.

editions.headline: Khamenei Laid to Rest in Mashhad as the Ceasefire He Died Over Stays Broken — Wall Street Looks Past It Toward SK Hynix
editions.teaser: Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is buried before dawn Friday at the Shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad, closing a six-day funeral that drew over 15 million mourners, while the US-Iran ceasefire remains broken and Pakistan and Qatar work back channels after two nights of renewed strikes; Wall Street shrugs it off, with Thursday's close (S&P +0.81% to 7,543.64, Nasdaq +1.30% to 26,206.89) setting up Friday's main event, SK Hynix's ~$26.5B Nasdaq debut, the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company; Delta tops Q2 estimates and reaffirms guidance; FOMC minutes show a 9-9 split with CME FedWatch now pricing 79% odds of a July hold; Bitcoin holds near $63,900 in a fragile bounce; Cubs (52-41) fall 3-2 to the Orioles missing the sweep, White Sox (47-44) are swept by Boston 2-1; today is the final day to file Form 843 Kwong refund claims.

editions.headline: Trump Says U.S. "Already Won Militarily" as Iran Buries Khamenei in Mashhad — Markets Shrug Off a Second Night of Strikes
editions.teaser: Iran buries Ali Khamenei today at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad as the six-day state funeral concludes, even as the U.S. struck 80+ Iranian targets overnight for a second straight night and Trump tells NATO allies in Ankara "we've already won militarily"; Wednesday's session was rough (Dow -1.09% to 52,348.39, S&P -0.28% to 7,482.71) but Thursday futures rise on chip-sector strength ahead of SK Hynix's ~$28B Nasdaq debut; FOMC June minutes show a 9-9 split on a 2026 hike, with Warsh withholding his own dot for the first time ever; Bitcoin holds near $62,850 in Extreme Fear; Cubs (52-40) slug past Orioles 9-7 on four homers while White Sox (47-44) are shut out 0-5 by Boston; final day tomorrow to file Form 843 Kwong COVID-era penalty refund claims.

editions.headline: Trump Declares Iran Ceasefire "Over" After U.S. Strikes 80+ Targets Overnight — Oil Surges 6%, Wall Street Braces for a Red Open
editions.teaser: President Trump declares the U.S.-Iran ceasefire "over" from the NATO summit in Ankara after Iran struck three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. retaliated with strikes on 80+ Iranian targets overnight; Iran hit U.S.-linked bases in Kuwait and Bahrain in response, with all projectiles intercepted; oil surges over 6% to a WTI price near $74.80 as Treasury reimposes Iran oil sanctions; U.S. equity futures fall broadly and gold slips despite the turmoil; FOMC minutes from the 9-9 split June meeting release at 2 PM ET; Cubs (51-40) beat Orioles Tuesday while White Sox (47-43) fall to the Red Sox.

editions.headline: Oil Tanker Struck Near Hormuz as Khamenei's Funeral Moves to Qom — Wall Street's Record Run Meets an Overnight Chip Wobble
editions.teaser: A tanker is struck near the Strait of Hormuz as UKMTO warns of renewed Iranian attacks in the waterway, just as Khamenei's funeral procession moves to Qom for prayers at the Jamkaran Mosque; Wall Street enters Tuesday fresh off Monday's record Dow close above 53,000, but Nasdaq 100 futures slip on a fresh Asia chip selloff ahead of Samsung earnings and SK Hynix's ~$28B Nasdaq listing; Bitcoin holds near $63,100; Microsoft cuts 4,800 jobs; Cubs (50-39) open at Baltimore and White Sox (47-42) host the Red Sox tonight.

editions.headline: Tehran's Biggest Day Yet: Khamenei's Main Funeral Procession Draws Immense Crowds as Wall Street Reopens to a Tech Rebound
editions.teaser: The largest single day of Ali Khamenei's six-day state funeral draws immense crowds toward Azadi Square in Tehran as Doha talks stay paused for funeral week; Wall Street reopens with Nasdaq 100 futures up 1% and S&P futures +0.4% after Thursday's record Dow close of 52,900.07 on a soft June jobs report; SK Hynix launches a ~$28B Nasdaq listing; Bitcoin eases to ~$62,900 off the weekend's $63K+ high; Cubs (50-39) beat Cardinals 6-4 to avoid the sweep, White Sox (47-42) split with Guardians; both teams off today.

editions.headline: Bitcoin Reclaims $63,000 as Khamenei's Funeral Enters a Second Day and Wall Street Waits Out a Quiet Weekend
editions.teaser: Bitcoin tops $63,000 for the first time in a month as ETF inflows resume and whales keep accumulating, even as markets stay dark until Monday behind Thursday's record Dow close of 52,900.07; the second day of Ali Khamenei's six-day state funeral draws thousands to Tehran's Grand Mosalla as Doha diplomacy remains paused for funeral week; the Cubs (49-39) and White Sox (46-42) both play series finales today looking to avoid weekend sweeps, and a stray shower risk lingers over Chicagoland behind Saturday's holiday storms.

editions.headline: America Turns 250: A Record-Shattering Fireworks Show and Historic Heat Mark the Semiquincentennial as Iran Pauses for a Funeral
editions.teaser: A record-attempt 850,000-shell fireworks display on the National Mall and historic heat headline America's 250th birthday, as Wall Street sits dark behind Thursday's record Dow close of 52,900.07 and Ali Khamenei's six-day state funeral begins in Tehran; the Cardinals rout the Cubs 17-1, the White Sox fight for first place in Cleveland, and evening storms threaten Chicagoland fireworks plans.

editions.headline: Markets Close Early for Independence Day as Iran Pauses Diplomacy and Cardinals Rout Cubs 17-1
editions.teaser: U.S. markets are closed in observance of July 4th after Thursday's record Dow close of 52,900.07; Iran suspends indirect Doha talks with the U.S. ahead of Ali Khamenei's six-day state funeral, which begins with his casket lying in state in Tehran; the Cardinals blast the Cubs 17-1 at Wrigley while the Guardians walk off the White Sox 4-3 in 10 innings to reclaim first place in the AL Central; Bitcoin holds in the high-$50,000s as whale accumulation continues.

editions.headline: Dow Rockets to a Record Close Above 52,900 as a Soft June Jobs Report Clears the Way for a Fed Pause
editions.teaser: The Dow jumps 594.83 points (+1.14%) to a record close of 52,900.07 after June nonfarm payrolls come in at just 57,000 versus 113,000 expected, even as unemployment ticks down to 4.2%; the S&P 500 is essentially flat at 7,483.24 while the Nasdaq falls 0.8% as chip stocks extend their slide and Tesla drops 7.5% despite beating delivery estimates; U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs snap a 10-day, $4.5 billion outflow streak with a $221.7 million inflow.

editions.headline: Dow Hits Intraday Record Above 52,700 Before Fading as Bitcoin Craters to a 21-Month Low
editions.teaser: The Dow surges to a fresh intraday record of 52,742.66 before slipping to close at 52,305.24 as Caterpillar and chip stocks pull back; Bending Spoons pops nearly 40% in its Nasdaq debut and Meta jumps 9% on cloud-business plans; Bitcoin tumbles to a 21-month low near $58,278 as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh tells the ECB's Sintra forum 'we've seen that prices are too high'; the first half of 2026 closes with the Dow up 8.9%, the S&P 500 up 9.6%, and the Russell 2000 up nearly 22% for its best half since 1991.

editions.headline: Stand-Down Holds, Doha Talks Open Today as Dow's Record Close Above 52,000 Sets the Tone for the Week
editions.teaser: The U.S. and Iran agree to stand down after a weekend Hormuz exchange, with technical talks shifting to Doha Tuesday; Monday's Dow closed above 52,000 for the first time (+306.63, 7,440.43 S&P), lifted by Alphabet's Dow debut, Rocket Lab's $8B Iridium deal, and a Supreme Court ruling preserving Fed Governor Lisa Cook's seat; Bitcoin lags below $60K; Cubs beat Padres 3-2, White Sox rout Orioles 8-2; Chicago under an Extreme Heat Warning through Thursday.

editions.headline: Dow Closes Above 52,000 for First Time as Supreme Court Preserves Fed Governor Cook's Seat
editions.teaser: The Dow closes above 52,000 for the first time ever as the Supreme Court's 5-4 ruling blocks Trump from firing Fed Governor Lisa Cook; Alphabet debuts in the Dow up nearly 5%; Rocket Lab announces $8B Iridium acquisition; Strategy authorizes its first-ever Bitcoin sell of up to $1.25B as BTC slides near $59,800; Cubs beat Padres 3-2, White Sox rout Orioles 8-2; Extreme heat warning issued for Chicagoland.

editions.headline: Iran Strikes Bahrain and Kuwait as US Resumes Attacks on Iranian Military Targets
editions.teaser: Iran launches retaliatory strikes on Bahrain and Kuwait after the US resumes attacks on Iranian military targets, with Trump warning of further escalation; oil and markets digest the renewed hostilities ahead of the week's Doha-track diplomacy.

editions.headline: OpenAI Delays IPO to 2027 as SpaceX Collapses 32% Post-Debut and the Nasdaq Logs a Fifth Straight Losing Session
editions.teaser: OpenAI pushes its IPO to 2027, SpaceX falls 32% from its debut high, and SoftBank drops 12.5% in a single session as the Nasdaq's losing streak extends to five days (week -4.6%); Bitcoin slides below $60,000 into Extreme Fear; White Sox rout Royals 22-1; Cubs drop the Milwaukee series opener 6-2; heat wave warning issued for the northwest suburbs.

editions.headline: Nasdaq and S&P 500 Tread Water Amid Tech Sell-Off, Reported OpenAI IPO Delay
editions.teaser: Markets tread water as reports surface that OpenAI is delaying its IPO; tech sell-off continues to pressure the Nasdaq amid ongoing Iran ceasefire dynamics and Fed rate uncertainty.

editions.headline: Micron Delivers Its Strongest Quarter in History — $41.46B Revenue, $50B Q4 Guidance, and a 17% Pop Rescue the AI Rally
editions.teaser: Micron's fiscal Q3 blowout — $41.46B revenue, $25.11 EPS, 84.9% gross margin — sends Nasdaq futures up 2% overnight and MU surging 17-18% on open; May PCE prints at 4.1% (3-year high) but in-line with estimates, analysts say May was the peak; Qualcomm +9%; Dansby Swanson sets Cubs franchise record with 11 RBI across a doubleheader sweep of the Mets (10-3, 10-5); Blackhawks trade #4 pick to Buffalo for Bowen Byram; NHL Draft Round 1 tonight in Buffalo.

editions.headline: All Eyes on Micron Tonight: Markets Attempt a Bounce After the AI Rout, But the HBM Number Will Decide Everything
editions.teaser: S&P 500 futures edge higher after Tuesday's brutal session (S&P −1.44%, Nasdaq −2.21%) as markets await Micron's fiscal Q3 earnings at 4:30 PM ET; Bulls land Caleb Wilson #4 and Dailyn Swain #15; Giannis traded to Miami; Alphabet joins the Dow Monday; BofA calls for three Fed hikes in 2026.

editions.headline: The AI Gravity Check: SpaceX Slides, Korea Craters, and the Nasdaq Faces Its Worst Day Since the IPO Selloff Began
editions.teaser: South Korea's KOSPI plunges 10%, Samsung and SK Hynix crater 12%+, SpaceX falls to $154.60 after its $20B bond sale, and Nasdaq futures drop 1.66% premarket; Bitcoin slips to $62,325; Oracle cuts 18,000 jobs citing AI; Micron earnings tomorrow; NBA Draft tonight with Bulls holding picks #4 and #15.

editions.headline: Starmer Out, Burnham In Line — The UK Gets Its 7th PM in a Decade as Bürgenstock Produces a 60-Day Roadmap
editions.teaser: Keir Starmer resigns as UK PM on Monday morning as the Bürgenstock talks yield a formal 60-day Iran nuclear roadmap; Bitcoin pops to $64K; Intel surges 10.6% on Apple chip deal; NBA Draft at Barclays tomorrow with Bulls holding picks #4 and #15.

editions.headline: Vance Meets Iranians Face-to-Face at Bürgenstock — The 60-Day Nuclear Clock Is Ticking
editions.teaser: JD Vance, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner sit across from Iran's delegation at Switzerland's Bürgenstock resort on Sunday, opening the 60-day nuclear sprint under the Islamabad MOU.

editions.headline: Bürgenstock Talks Stumble Out of the Gate — Then Resume: The Iran MOU's First 48 Hours Are a Preview of What's Ahead
editions.teaser: After Friday's abrupt postponement, US-Iran implementation talks resume Saturday at Bürgenstock with Witkoff and Kushner on-site.

editions.headline: Juneteenth 2026: Markets Pause, Bürgenstock Talks Begin, and Bitcoin Slides Into a Hawkish Long Weekend
editions.teaser: NYSE, Nasdaq, and bond markets are dark for Juneteenth as Thursday's equity recovery rally (S&P +1.08% to 7,500.58) locks in a split verdict for the week.

editions.headline: Signed, Sealed, Delivered at Versailles: Trump and Pezeshkian Sign the Iran MOU as Markets Shrug Off Warsh's Hawkish Shock
editions.teaser: Trump and Iran's Pezeshkian sign the war-ending memorandum at the Palace of Versailles, sending stocks sharply higher even as Wednesday's hawkish Fed dot plot rattled bond markets.

editions.headline: Decision Day: Warsh Delivers His First Rate Verdict at 2 PM as Bond Market Bets Shift From Cuts to Hikes
editions.teaser: Kevin Warsh's first FOMC decision lands at 2 PM with a hold all but certain, but the dot plot and his debut press conference will show how a divided committee is leaning.

editions.headline: Kevin Warsh's Fed Era Begins: First FOMC Meeting Opens Today as Inflation Runs Hot and Trump Says He 'Loved' It
editions.teaser: Kevin Warsh opens his first FOMC meeting as fed chair with a rate hold expected, May CPI at 4.2%, and Monday's Iran-deal rally still echoing through fresh record closes.

editions.headline: 'The Deal With Iran Is Now Complete': Trump Authorizes Reopening of Strait of Hormuz, Markets Surge to Start the Week
editions.teaser: Trump declares the U.S.-Iran deal 'now complete' and authorizes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, sending Dow futures up 463 points.

editions.headline: Qatari Mediators Race to Tehran as Trump Declares Hormuz Deal 'Scheduled' for His Birthday
editions.teaser: Qatari mediators race to Tehran for a potential breakthrough as Trump says a Hormuz-related deal is 'scheduled' to land on his birthday; S&P 500 rises 1.75% to 7,394.30.

editions.headline: 'Peace Has Never Been This Close': Pakistan Says U.S.-Iran Deal Text Finalized, Signing Could Come Within 24 Hours
editions.teaser: Pakistan says a finalized U.S.-Iran deal text could be signed within 24 hours as the S&P 500 rises 0.5% to close just shy of 7,400.

editions.headline: SpaceX Roars Onto Nasdaq in Largest IPO Ever as Iran Deal Optimism Lifts Wall Street
editions.teaser: SpaceX debuts on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX in the largest IPO in corporate history, raising roughly $75 billion, as Iran deal optimism lifts the Dow 354 points to 51,202.

editions.headline: Trump Cancels Iran Strikes — Markets Surge; Tornado Outbreak Hits Chicago
editions.teaser: Trump cancels planned Iran strikes, sending the Dow up 930 points (+1.86%) and the S&P 500 up 1.75%, as a tornado outbreak hits northern Illinois and NW Indiana.

editions.headline: Dow Sheds 953 Points as CPI Hits Three-Year High — US Resumes Iran Strikes
editions.teaser: Dow drops 953 points below the 50,000 floor and Nasdaq falls 1.98% as May CPI hits a three-year high of 4.2% and the US resumes strikes on Iran.

editions.headline: U.S. Launches Self-Defense Strikes on Iran as Markets Reel; Nasdaq, S&P Plunge on Tech Selloff
editions.teaser: The U.S. launches self-defense strikes on Iran as the Nasdaq and S&P 500 fall roughly 1% amid a renewed tech selloff.

editions.headline: Chip Stocks Rebound; Nasdaq and Russell 2000 Book Small Comeback After Friday's Rout
editions.teaser: Chip stocks rebound and S&P 500 futures rise 0.4% premarket as easing Iran hostilities help markets recover from Friday's 4%+ Nasdaq rout.

editions.headline: Week Ends on Sour Note: Nasdaq Falls 4.7% as Chip Selloff Accelerates on Hot Jobs Data
editions.teaser: Nasdaq falls roughly 4.7% for the week as a hot May jobs report (172,000 vs. consensus) reignites fears the Fed will hold rates higher for longer.

editions.headline: Chips Crater — Nasdaq Suffers Worst Day Since April 2025 as Broadcom Disappoints
editions.teaser: Nasdaq plunges 4.18% — its worst session since April 2025 — as Broadcom's guidance disappoints and chip stocks lead a broad selloff to S&P 7,383.74.

editions.headline: S&P Breaks 7,600 for First Time — Dow Hits All-Time High as Rotation Lifts Defensives
editions.teaser: S&P 500 closes at a record 7,584.31, breaking 7,600 intraday, as defensive sectors lead a rotation-driven rally to fresh Dow highs.

editions.headline: Dow Smashes Record +1.73% as Chips Drag Nasdaq — Rotation Accelerates Into Jobs Friday
editions.teaser: Dow Jones surges 874 points (+1.73%) to a fresh record as a rotation out of chip stocks accelerates ahead of Friday's jobs report.

editions.headline: Iran Drones Kuwait's Airport — Ceasefire Collapses, Oil Spikes, Stocks Fall
editions.teaser: The four-day Iran ceasefire collapses after drone strikes on Kuwait International Airport; oil spikes to $97.80 and Bitcoin falls to $67,200.

editions.headline: Markets Reverse From Records — Bitcoin Plunges 31% in 9 Days as Saylor Breaks 'Never Sell' Pledge
editions.teaser: S&P 500 falls 0.74% from its record as Bitcoin plunges to $72,400, down 31% in nine days, after Strategy's Michael Saylor breaks his 'never sell' pledge.

editions.headline: Iran MOU Signed — Markets Surge to New Records as Ceasefire Takes Effect
editions.teaser: S&P 500 hits 7,621 and the Dow crosses 51,188 as a signed Iran memorandum of understanding sends markets to fresh records.

editions.headline: Month-End Recap: May 2026 Was One for the History Books — What June Holds
editions.teaser: A look back at a record-setting May 2026 and a preview of what June has in store for markets, the Fed, and geopolitics.

editions.headline: May Ends at Records Across the Board — Dow Crosses 51,000 for the First Time
editions.teaser: Dow Jones crosses 51,000 for the first time ever as May closes out with records across major indices.

editions.headline: S&P Hits Record Close as Iran Deal Framework Signals Ceasefire — PCE Inflation Complicates Fed Math
editions.teaser: S&P 500 closes at record 7,609 as Iran ceasefire framework emerges from Oman talks; PCE inflation comes in hot at 3.8%.

editions.headline: Markets Shrug Off Iran Headlines — Dow Hits Second Consecutive Record Close
editions.teaser: Dow notches second straight record close at 50,516 as Warsh confirmation odds rise and Iran ceasefire talks continue in Oman.

editions.headline: Dow Surges to Record as Chips Dump — Warsh Nomination Rattles Bond Market
editions.teaser: Dow Jones gains 282 points to a record 50,234 even as chip stocks slump and the Warsh Fed nomination pushes the 10-year yield to 4.52%.
